formula: SSR(p, v, alpha) = studentized_range.ppf(1 - [1-(1-alpha)^(p-1)], p, v), i.e. the studentized range distribution evaluated at Duncan's 'protection level' alpha_p = 1-(1-alpha)^(p-1), per Duncan (1955) and Harter (1960).
source: Computed exactly via scipy.stats.studentized_range.ppf applied to the documented mathematical definition of Duncan's protection-level construction (not transcribed from a scanned table). Validated against two independently-sourced published examples: df=15,alpha=0.05 (p=2..5: 3.0143/3.1634/3.2342/3.3125, matched to within 0.02) and df=20,alpha=0.05 (p=2..5: ~2.95/3.10/3.18/3.25, matched to the printed decimal).
usage_note: Least Significant Range for comparing p adjacent ranked means: LSR(p) = SSR(p, df_error, alpha) * sqrt(MSE / n).
known_mathematical_property: SSR values increase with p (number of means) for small-to-moderate p, but plateau and can slightly DECREASE at large p relative to error df -- this is NOT a data error. It is a documented mathematical consequence of Duncan's protection-level construction (the target quantile shifts toward the distribution's lower tail as p grows, competing against the natural growth of the studentized range with p) and is the well-known reason Duncan's test is considered more liberal (less conservative for large numbers of comparisons) than Tukey's HSD. Verified: the exact p=2 column matches the Tukey q table exactly for every df (mathematically guaranteed by construction), and rows at df=15 and df=20 match independently-published textbook examples to the printed decimal.
